title: An accept deletes the merged branch even when it is ahead of its pushed copy
name: accept-branch-delete
description: Seen on 2026-09-24 in backup-attend-osc2. `deleteBranch` in packages/core/src/merge.ts:67 runs `git branch -d`. When a branch has an upstream, `-d` checks that the branch is merged into that upstream, not into HEAD. A node branch that was pushed for its draft PR and then got local commits (a merge from the base, a fix-up) is merged into the base but is ahead of `origin/sober/<node>`. So `-d` refuses, the `accept` tool returns `git branch -d … failed`, and the merge, the worktree removal and the done mark have already happened. The user sees an error for an accept that succeeded. Fix: after the merge, check `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> HEAD` and then delete with `-D`. Only a branch that is not in HEAD is refused, with a clear sentence. Test in packages/core/src/merge.test.ts (or the file that holds the accept tests): a branch with an upstream it is ahead of, merged into the base, is deleted with no error.

brief.approach:
The bug is in `deleteBranch` (packages/core/src/merge.ts:62). It runs `git branch -d`. When the branch has an upstream (set by `publish` in packages/core/src/pr.ts:108 with `push -u`), `-d` checks the branch against that upstream, not HEAD. A node branch pushed for its draft PR and then given a local commit is ahead of `origin/sober/<node>`, so `-d` refuses — after `acceptWork` (packages/core/src/review.ts:141) has already merged, recorded the node as done and removed the worktree.

Fix, in packages/core/src/merge.ts only:
1. In `deleteBranch`, when `force` is not set, run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> HEAD` in `paths.root`. The local-merge path in review.ts:214 calls it right after `mergeNode`, while `paths.root` is on the base, so HEAD is the base.
2. If it is an ancestor, delete with `git branch -D`. The ancestry check is the safety `-d` gave; `-D` only skips the upstream comparison.
3. If it is not an ancestor, throw `MergeRefusedError` with a clear sentence: the branch holds commits the base does not have, so it is kept.
4. `force: true` (the pull-request landing, review.ts:204) keeps its current behaviour: `-D` with no check.
5. Update the doc comment on `deleteBranch` to say why `-d` is not used.

No change to review.ts is needed: the call sites stay the same.

Test: add one case to test/integration/pr.test.ts, next to "accept lands locally by default". That file already has a real bare remote, `board()` and `publish()` (which pushes with `-u`). The case: `board()`, `publish(paths, 'auth-api-k7f2', 'main')`, then add a second commit in the node's worktree (so the branch is ahead of its pushed copy), then `acceptWork(... base: 'main', scan: 'clean')`. It must resolve with `kind: 'merged'`, main's log contains `sober: auth-api-k7f2`, and `git branch --list sober/auth-api-k7f2` is empty. The declared file packages/core/src/merge.test.ts does not exist; the integration file is where the accept tests with a remote live, so the test goes there instead.

acceptance.proves: The new case passes: a branch pushed with an upstream, then committed to locally, is accepted with no error and its branch is gone; the existing accept and pull-request cases still pass.

acceptance.run: pnpm vitest run --project integration loop.test.ts cli.test.ts mcp.test.ts
acceptance.proves: The other accept paths (plain local merge with no upstream, CLI and MCP accept) still merge and delete the branch.
The change passes biome and secretlint.
